questions.question: OP-01/O14: D35 says a stream read surfaces "only" unavailable, timeout, changed, base, auth failed and caller errors. But a resume (D39) is a new request that can meet E6/E15, and D20/D33 let cancellation and memory/descriptor failures out of a read. What may a stream read surface?

options.label: Widen (Recommended)
options.description: Every D34 category except key refused, not found, not an item (classification is the open's, D22) and decode (the stream is binary). Adds permission denied, not readable, as-raised failures, cancellation. Source: OP-01/O14.

options.label: Narrow D19
options.description: Keep D35's list; D19's s3 cells for E6 and E15 become '—'. A resume that meets E6/E15 then needs another category (e.g. unavailable), which misleads the fix.

options.label: Widen, no E15
options.description: Widen as recommended but leave E15 out of the read phase; E15 during a stream then surfaces as whatever O15 decides at the open only.

questions.question: OP-01/O26(iii) + O39: D35's open-call list lacks unavailable and timeout (D28), a cancelled open (D20), caller errors before contact and E13's base category and as-raised failures (D33). What may the stream's open surface?

options.label: All but changed (Recommended)
options.description: Every D34 category except changed (nothing is pinned yet) and decode (binary). A whole read surfaces every D34 row at its one call, as D35 says. Source: OP-01/O26, O39.

options.label: Add only O26's two
options.description: Add unavailable and timeout; cancellation, caller errors and E13 stay unlisted at the open, so the spec clause for the open stays incomplete.

questions.question: OP-01/O15: D25 puts E15 (archive tier, missing customer key) under 'pinned or fails changed', but its dialog asked about E3/E5 only, and D30 types E15 as not readable. A tier change keeps the content (and its ETag, not run). What does E15 do to an open stream?

options.label: Not readable (Recommended)
options.description: E15 leaves D25. A stream continues while its transfer holds; a read needing a new request (resume) fails not readable, stream Failed. Content was not changed, so changed would mislead. Source: OP-01/O15, D30.

options.label: Changed
options.description: E15 stays in D25: the stream fails changed. One category for every 'cannot keep serving', but the caller retries a read that will fail not readable.

questions.question: OP-01/O33: D34's changed row reads 'E1 to E5 against a pinned stream', E4 (in-place modification) included, while D26 says under E4 pinning is not promised and rejects detection that fails changed. Does E4 leave the row?

options.label: E4 leaves (Recommended)
options.description: Changed row: E1, E2, E3, E5 (and what O44 adds). Under E4 a read surfaces no category of its own and may end short without failing (D26). Source: D26, OP-01/O33.

options.label: E4 may surface changed
options.description: Keep E4 as 'may' fail changed, leaving room for best-effort detection that D26 rejected; a test can then assert neither outcome.

options.label: Yes, propagates (Recommended)
options.description: E14's s4 cell becomes 'yes'; D19's sentence reads 's4 reports nothing but a cancellation'. Swallowing CancelledError breaks asyncio task cancellation. Source: OP-01/O16, D36, asyncio's rule that CancelledError propagates.

options.label: No, close swallows it
options.description: D36 amended: close() raises nothing at all. A task cancelled during await close() then does not see its cancellation there; asyncio's TaskGroup and timeouts can hang or misbehave.

questions.question: OP-01/O45: D20 makes a cancelled stream read release the stream (Closed), but D18's transition table has no column for it, and D20's check names only Open. Is it shown in D18's table?

options.label: Add a column (Recommended)
options.description: D18's table gains 'a read is cancelled': Closed in every row (Closed stays Closed). D20's check names every state, as its Decision does. One table holds every transition. Source: OP-01/O45, D20.

options.label: Leave it in D20
options.description: The spec writes the transition from D20's sentence; D18's table stays partial, as its own text says ('Cancellation is AX-7's').

questions.question: OP-01/O36: D18 says 'a failure moves to Failed', so literally chunks(0) (a caller ValueError) would leave the stream Failed and every later read re-raise it. Which failures move Open to Failed?

options.label: All but caller/cancel (Recommended)
options.description: Every storage failure and every as-raised failure (MemoryError, descriptors) moves to Failed; a caller error is raised before any effect and leaves the state unchanged; a cancellation moves to Closed (D20). Source: OP-01/O36, D16, D33.

options.label: Storage failures only
options.description: Only D27's categories move to Failed; an as-raised MemoryError leaves the stream Open although bytes may already be lost from the transfer, so the next read could return bytes after a gap, against D6/D16.

options.label: As-raised to Closed
options.description: Storage failures to Failed; MemoryError/descriptor failures to Closed like a cancellation. The original failure is then lost to code that reads on (what D16 rejected Closed for).

questions.question: OP-01/O26(ii), AX-6: D16's Failed state raises 'the same failure again'. Is that the same exception object re-raised, or a new one?

options.label: New, chained (Recommended)
options.description: A new exception of the same category each time, the original as its __cause__. Fresh traceback per raise; re-raising one object grows its __traceback__ on every raise. Callers compare by category, never by identity. Source: PEP 3134 (chaining).

options.label: Same object
options.description: The stored exception is raised again: identity holds (`is` works, Go bufio's sticky error), but its traceback accumulates frames from every raise and keeps them alive.

OP-01/O17: D33 types so that `except` on the store's base never hides a caller's bug, yet D34 puts key refused (often a caller bug) under that base (and ValueError). Where does key refused sit?

options.label: Base + ValueError (Recommended)
options.description: Keep D34. Narrow D33's reason to 'caller errors no store configuration decides'. A refusal depends on the store's L_api (KEY-001, KEY-008): one input passes on one store, fails on another, so it is the store's verdict. Source: KEY-008, OP-01/O17.

options.label: ValueError only
options.description: Key refused is a caller error, outside the store's base. `except StoreError` no longer catches it; code taking untrusted names must also catch ValueError, which hides other bugs.

questions.question: OP-01/O22: descriptor exhaustion (E13) propagates as raised OSError on Local, but through an SDK it looks like a failed connect, which D28 types unavailable and D38 retries. One category on every backend, or not?

options.label: Unspecified of two (Recommended)
options.description: F3 'unspecified': descriptor exhaustion surfaces as raised or as unavailable, on any backend. Honest, checkable, no cause-chain digging. Memory stays as raised. Source: OP-01/O22, axes.md F3.

options.label: Normalise to raised
options.description: The library searches the cause chain for EMFILE/ENFILE and re-raises the OSError on every backend. Rests on every SDK chaining causes, which none promises.

options.label: Profile-declared
options.description: A variation point per backend (AX-15). But it varies by SDK internals, not by backend semantics, and adds a profile row.

questions.question: OP-01/O26(i): an unknown `encoding` (or `errors` handler) raises LookupError, which is outside D33's caller errors (TypeError, ValueError). What does the text form do?

options.label: LookupError, early (Recommended)
options.description: LookupError as raised, checked before any backend contact (codecs.lookup, codecs.lookup_error); D33's caller errors become TypeError, ValueError, LookupError. Same as bytes.decode and open(). Source: OP-01/O26.

options.label: Wrap as ValueError
options.description: Converted to ValueError before contact. Keeps D33's list, but differs from what decode() and open() raise.

options.label: LookupError, late
options.description: Raised when decoding, after the transfer. A misspelt encoding costs a full download first.

options.description: D28/D34: E7's connect past T_connect surfaces as timeout (an unavailable, TimeoutError); refused or unresolvable as unavailable. E7 stays one row. botocore and aiohttp also keep the two apart. Source: OP-01/O27, D12.

options.label: Unavailable
options.description: D12 amended: a slow connect is unavailable; only E9's idle stall is timeout. `except TimeoutError` then misses a slow connect.

options.label: Base + ValueError (Recommended)

options.description: Key refused is a caller error, outside the store's base. `except StoreError` no longer catches it; code taking untrusted names must also catch ValueError, which hides other bugs.
options.label: ValueError only

questions.question: OP-01/O17: D33 types so that `except` on the store's base never hides a caller's bug, yet D34 puts key refused (often a caller bug) under that base (and ValueError). Where does key refused sit?

options.description: F3 'unspecified': descriptor exhaustion surfaces as raised or as unavailable, on any backend. Honest, checkable, no cause-chain digging. Memory stays as raised. Source: OP-01/O22, axes.md F3.

options.description: The library searches the cause chain for EMFILE/ENFILE and re-raises the OSError on every backend. Rests on every SDK chaining causes, which none promises.
options.label: Normalise to raised

options.description: A variation point per backend (AX-15). But it varies by SDK internals, not by backend semantics, and adds a profile row.
options.label: Profile-declared

options.description: Raised when decoding, after the transfer. A misspelt encoding costs a full download first.

OP-01/O41: name resolution (getaddrinfo) takes no timeout in CPython, urllib3 or paramiko, so the sync form cannot bound it by T_connect without a helper thread, the cost D14 rejected for Local I/O. How is resolution bounded?

options.label: Declared deviation (Recommended)
options.description: D43's Termination row gains: name resolution ends when the system resolver returns (every network backend, both forms alike, per D1). T_connect counts from the connect after resolution. Same reasoning as D14. Source: OP-01/O41, D14.

options.label: T_connect covers it
options.description: Resolution runs in a helper thread (sync) or the executor (async) and is bounded by T_connect; a timed-out lookup leaves a thread behind until the resolver returns.

options.label: Async only
options.description: The async form bounds resolution by T_connect (executor), the sync form deviates. Breaks D1's parity: one caller code path waits differently per form.

questions.question: OP-01/O23 (AX-5's caller deadline): with no whole-call deadline (D12), a caller's own deadline is a cancellation, and D20 closes a stream whose read is cancelled. Does D12 record that trade-off?

options.label: Record it (Recommended)
options.description: D12 gains: a caller imposes their own deadline by cancelling (E14), e.g. asyncio.timeout; a whole read hands out nothing, a stream read's deadline costs the stream (D20), so a caller wanting to go on makes a new call. Answers AX-5's added question. Source: OP-01/O23, axes.md AX-5.

options.label: As is
options.description: D12 and D20 stand unchanged; the spec derives the trade-off from both. AX-5's caller-deadline question stays answered only implicitly.

questions.question: OP-01/O32: D12's and D38's checks say AX-13 bounds a call's total waiting, but D39 restarts the retry limit once bytes flow, so one stream read(-1) may resume any number of times. Narrow both checks?

options.label: Narrow (Recommended)
options.description: Both checks read: waiting is bounded per request and, for a whole read, per call (attempt limit × bound + backoff); a stream's total is not bounded while bytes keep flowing (D39, NP1). Source: OP-01/O32.

options.label: As is
options.description: Keep the checks; the spec writes from D12's Decision and NP1/NP2, which already hold. The checks stay wrong for streams.

questions.question: OP-01/O37: D38's caller-level retry table lacks rows for a decode failure (D32), caller errors and as-raised failures (D33), and a cancellation (D20). Which rows?

options.label: Four rows (Recommended)
options.description: Decode under strict: repeats it unless the content changes (D5). Caller error: repeats it (a function of the arguments). Memory/descriptors as raised: may succeed once resources free. Cancellation: a new call is unaffected by it. Source: OP-01/O37.

options.label: Out of scope
options.description: D38's table covers storage failures only; a note says the others are not the store's. The spec then has no clause for retrying them.

OP-01/O28: D22/D25/D34 say a lost pin fails 'changed' with no exception, while D42/D43 give a backend that cannot pin (SFTP, an undeclared S3 endpoint) 'no resume: fails unavailable'. There the library cannot know whether the content changed. How do the two read together?

options.label: Normal value only (Recommended)
options.description: D22, D25, D34's changed row state the normal value; under D43's no-resume deviation a dropped stream fails unavailable, as D42 decided. D38's unavailable row notes a new call reads the content current at its own open. Claiming 'changed' without knowing would be false. Source: OP-01/O28, D42.

options.label: Changed there too
options.description: Where the backend cannot pin, a drop fails changed, since the content might have changed. Callers never mistake it for retryable, but get false positives on every network blip.

options.label: Own category
options.description: A third category, 'cannot resume', under unavailable: tells 'restart from 0' apart from both. One more category for every entry's error layer.

questions.question: OP-01/O44: no Environment row covers O3 changing only an item's metadata. On Azure that gives a new ETag, so a pinned resume fails 'changed' though the content is the open's; on S3 a metadata-only change keeps the ETag (session input). What then?

options.label: Row + deviation (Recommended)
options.description: Add E-row: O3 changes an item's metadata or properties, not its content. Changed means the pin token changed; D43's Pinned resume row declares a deviation: a metadata-only change also fails a resume changed (Azure; not run). D31's reason reads 'the current content, which may equal the old'. Source: OP-01/O44.

options.label: Row, no deviation
options.description: Add the row, but promise a metadata-only change never fails a resume. Azure would then need a pin token other than the ETag, which it does not offer in general.

questions.question: OP-01/O31: D25's dialog adopted 'D21 to D23 apply unchanged' for O3, but its Decision added that D23's real-time order holds only for API mutations, an O3 change visible when the backend says, with no variation point or non-promise row. Which?

options.label: D23 applies to O3 (Recommended)
options.description: D25's sentence dropped: once O3's change completes (its tool returned), a later OP-01 sees it, under D23's normal value and declared deviations. Testable with a native SDK writer; holds natively on S3, Azure, Local. Source: OP-01/O31, D25's adopted option.

options.label: Non-promise
options.description: Register: when an O3 change becomes visible is not promised (scope E3, E5, E15). Simple, but a caller syncing with other tools gets no guarantee anywhere.

options.label: Own variation point
options.description: A separate AX-15 point for O3 visibility, its own normal value and deviations; one more row OP-18 must expose.

questions.question: OP-01/O43: Local on NFS, two hosts: after O2's rename on one host the other may open the old file until its attribute cache expires (against D23); another host's rm can make the open descriptor fail ESTALE (D25's reason). What does Local declare?

options.label: Static deviation (Recommended)
options.description: D43's Read-after-write row: Local on a network file system, across hosts: eventual. A stream whose file another host removes fails changed (ESTALE), D22's normal value, so pinning needs no deviation. Source: OP-01/O43; NFS close-to-open (RFC 7530), not run.

options.label: Outside the profile
options.description: A registered non-promise: D23 and D25 across hosts on a network file system are not promised. Smaller, but leaves ESTALE's category open.

options.label: Config-selected
options.description: Per D43's rule, the caller declares a network FS in configuration. An unnamed (default) Local store then gets the deviation, penalising every local-disk user.

options.description: D35's whole-read sentence reads as D79 does. D46's open list also leaves out a closed stream's ValueError. D46's check reads: the two lists overlap in what any backend request can meet, the caller errors raised before contact, and a cancellation.

options.label: D79 governs, texts stay
options.description: D35 and D46 are left as they are, and D79 is read as superseding them. A spec author then meets two texts that disagree.
